g.text: Every layer below exists to reject the same ~499,000 requests as cheaply as possible.
arrive within roughly 5 seconds of sale-open
they hold a queue position at the waiting-room gate instead
Admitted, a bounded number at a time
rate-limited per user/IP so no single script hogs a slot
One script or IP can't consume a disproportionate
share of the gate's admitted slots
Every admitted attempt checks the counter
one atomic in-memory operation -- no database call
999 of every 1,000 checks past this point still fail
for the cost of one Redis operation -- not a database row lock
the only writes the DB ever makes
The gate, the rate limiter, and the in-memory counter all exist for one reason:
make sure the database only ever has to answer 1,000 questions, never 500,000.
